Create a 2D dam-break simulation case for OpenFOAM using the interFoam solver with a sharp VOF interface tracking method.
The computational domain is 1 m in x, 1 m in y, and one cell thick in z.
The mesh has 40 cells in x, 80 cells in y, and 1 cell in z, giving uniform cell sizes of 0.025 m in x and 0.0125 m in y.
The frontAndBack patches in z are set to empty type.
The bottom wall (y=0) and left wall (x=0) are wall-type boundary patches.
The top boundary (y=1 m) and right boundary (x=1 m) are atmosphere-type (or empty/zeroGradient pressure) boundary patches.
In system/controlDict, set the application to interFoam.
Initialize the fields using setFields: set alpha.water to 1 inside the rectangular region 0 <= x <= 0.25 m and 0 <= y <= 0.57 m, and alpha.water to 0 everywhere else.
The initial velocity field is zero throughout the domain.
Use standard interFoam physical properties: water density 1000 kg/m3, air density 1 kg/m3, kinematic viscosity 1e-6 m2/s for water and 1.5e-5 m2/s for air, gravity vector (0, -9.81, 0) m/s2.
Use a small time step (deltaT = 0.0001) with adjustable time stepping (adjustTimeStep yes, maxCo = 0.5) and an endTime of 0.6 s.
The case directory structure follows standard OpenFOAM layout: constant/ (transportProperties, gravity, g), system/ (controlDict, fvSchemes, fvSolution), 0/ (alpha.water, U, p), and a generated mesh.
